title: Growth meets a cost shock.
summary: The economy is still expanding. The next test is whether energy, inflation, and borrowing costs erode that resilience.
marketStatus: U.S. closed Monday · next regular open Tue, Sept 8, 9:30 a.m. ET

changes.title: Start of the record
changes.body: This is the first entry. Daily changes will compare with a real prior snapshot; no historical entries are fabricated.

changes.title: Consumer data needs context
changes.body: Card delinquency flows remain roughly stable. The fall in total debt partly reflects a mortgage-reporting gap.

changes.title: Prepare for inflation week
changes.body: August PPI and CPI precede the September 15–16 Fed meeting.

topics.title: Energy & conflict
topics.headline: War reaches markets through fuel, freight, and household purchasing power.
topics.mechanism: Reported supply disruptions and rising fuel prices increase costs before the full effect appears in company earnings.
topics.falsifier: Physical supply recovery would weaken this risk; diplomatic headlines alone are insufficient.

topics.title: Rates & liquidity
topics.headline: Positive growth does not guarantee falling interest rates.
topics.mechanism: Higher real yields raise the hurdle for long-duration earnings, debt refinancing and investment.
topics.falsifier: Sustained disinflation and improved bond demand would ease pressure.

topics.title: Consumer & credit
topics.headline: New missed payments are roughly stable, while some households remain strained.
topics.mechanism: The flow into serious delinquency differs from the stock of overdue debt. Mortgage-reporting gaps distort total debt.
topics.falsifier: Worsening new delinquencies alongside weaker real spending would change the view.

topics.title: Inflation & jobs
topics.headline: A cooler monthly inflation print does not restore old price levels.
topics.mechanism: Energy and financing compete with discretionary spending even as payrolls grow.
topics.falsifier: Look for broad, sustained cooling and stronger real incomes.

topics.title: Earnings & AI
topics.headline: Aggregate earnings expectations improved, but not across every sector.
topics.mechanism: Investment-accounting gains and heavy AI spending require a cash-flow check.
topics.falsifier: Broader operating growth and cash conversion would strengthen confidence.

topics.title: International
topics.headline: Europe, China, and Japan transmit different demand and financing risks.
topics.mechanism: Energy costs, manufacturing orders and exchange rates affect U.S. multinational margins.
topics.falsifier: Verify stronger final demand and actual supply recovery before assuming normalization.

query.sql: WITH reviewed(category, period, rate) AS (VALUES ('Credit cards','Q2 2025',6.93),('Credit cards','Q2 2026',6.97),('Auto loans','Q2 2025',2.93),('Auto loans','Q2 2026',3.0),('Mortgages','Q2 2025',1.29),('Mortgages','Q2 2026',1.52),('HELOCs','Q2 2025',1.15),('HELOCs','Q2 2026',1.15),('Student loans','Q2 2025',12.88),('Student loans','Q2 2026',7.83)) SELECT category, period, rate, 'Annualized balance flow into 90+ days delinquent; percent' AS definition FROM reviewed
metric_definitions: Annualized balance flow into 90+ days delinquent; numeric values are percentage points, e.g. 6.97 means 6.97%.
